newsitem.title: UK: Top 10 sugar exporters key to global balance - Man.
newsitem.headline: Top 10 sugar exporters key to global balance - Man.

text.p: Sugar exports from a small group of the world's top 10 exporters will pressure world prices in the near to medium term but the situation could easily reverse by second quarter 1997, trade house E D & F Man said on Tuesday.
Sugar surpluses or shortages on the world market were being increasingly determined by a small group of countries, it said in a monthly report.
Exports of the top 10 sugar exporters which accounted for 80 percent of total exports on the world market would rise by four million tonnes during the 1995/97 (October/September) period.

Total world market imports were expected to rise only marginally during this period and thus put the accumulated exportable surplus at 3.9 million tonnes, more than half of which would be in white sugar, Man said.

"The balance of such a surplus based largely on sugar that has already been exported or committed for export should put a near to medium pressure on prices but this situation can easily be turned around by second quarter next year," the report said. "In the current market situation, even minor hiccups in the production of the major sugar exporting countries would upset the overall fundamental balance."
